MAYO HALL UNIT, BENGALURU (SCCH-19),
AWARDING COMPENSATION OF RS.5,72,500/- WITH INTEREST AT 6 PERCENT P.A. (EXCLUDING FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES)
FROM THE DATE OF PETITION TILL ITS REALIZATION.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed by the appellant under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 challenging the judgment and award dated 08.12.2022 passed in MVC No.5439/2021 by the Court of XV Additional, Small Causes Judge and XXIII ACMM, Bengaluru (SCCH-19) (hereinafter referred to as the 'Tribunal').
2.
Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the appellant.
The respondent remained absent.
3. The status of the parties before the Tribunal is retained for the sake of convenience.

4. The case of the appellant/claimant is that she filed a claim petition before the Tribunal under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act (for short 'M.V. Act') claiming NC: 2024:KHC:21371 compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by her in a road traffic accident that occurred on 19.11.2021 at about 9.42 a.m. that the petitioner was traveling as a pillion rider in a motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-53/HB-3721 towards Whitefield main road, at that time, BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-53/F-0033 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motor cycle.
Due to which, the claimant fell down and sustained grievous injuries as well as crush injury.
Immediately after the accident, she was shifted to Manipal Hospital, wherein she took treatment and underwent surgery.
Due to the accidental injuries, she sustained disability and has incurred huge medical expenses and loss of discomfort.
Therefore, the claimant filed the petition seeking compensation on various grounds.

5. The respondent-Insurance Company appeared before the Tribunal and filed statement of objections contending that the accident was occurred due to negligent riding of the motor cycle and the motor cycle NC: 2024:KHC:21371 trying to overtake the bus on the left side, due to which, the accident was occurred.
The petition also bad for non- joinder of necessary parties and also disputed the manner of accident, age, income, medical expenses incurred and disability and prayed for dismissal of the suit.

sentences.text:
On the basis of pleadings, the tribunal framed the following issues for consideration:
1. Whether the Petitioner proves that on 19.11.2021 at about 9.42 a.m. the petitioner was traveling as a pillion rider in a Motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-53/HB-3721 ridden by its rider carefully and cautiously, proceeding on Whitefield main road,
when reached in front of TATA Elexi Apartment, Bangalore, at that time, driver of one BMTC Bus bearing reg.No.KA- 53/F-0033 drove the same, in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life, came at high speed and dashed the petitioner's vehicle and caused the accident.

As a result of forced impact,
the petitioner sustained grievous injuries?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
NC: 2024:KHC:21371 3.
What order or award?
7. In order to prove the case of the petitioner, the petitioner examined herself as PW.1 and also got examined the doctor as PW.2 and got marked documents as Exs.P1 to P17.

On the other hand,
examined the driver of the bus as RW.1 and the Medical Officer was examined as RW.2 and got marked documents as Exs.R1 to R5.
8.

On the basis of material evidence, both oral and documentary and on hearing the submissions of learned counsel for both parties, the tribunal answered issue No.1 in the affirmative and issue No.2 partly in the affirmative and the tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.5,72,500/- with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization and also held the respondent is liable to pay the compensation to the claimant and directed to deposit the amount together with 6% interest within 60 days from the date of award.
NC: 2024:KHC:21371 9.
Being aggrieved by the meager compensation awarded by the tribunal, the claimant is before this Court challenging the impugned judgment and award.

10. It is the vehement contention of the learned counsel for appellant that the award passed by the tribunal is excessive and exorbitant including the income considered on various heads, the tribunal granted excessive and the permanent disability considered as 11% to the whole body, which is not correct.
The doctor who examined has issued disability certificate, but he was not treated.
The doctor had assessed the disability to the extent of 39% to the right arm, which is not correct.

The discomfort mentioned by the doctor - PW.2 is not in accordance with the guidelines and hence,
prayed for reducing the compensation awarded by the tribunal.

3 11.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Having heard the learned counsel for appellant and on perusal of the Exs.P1 to P17, the point to be considered is as follows:
NC: 2024:KHC:21371 'Whether the award of compensation passed by the tribunal is excessive and exorbitant to the facts and circumstances of the case and requires for reduction, if so advised?'
12.

On perusal of the records, the accident was occurred on 19.11.2021 at about 9.42 a.m., which is disputed by the respondent driver contending that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the motor cycle, but not due to negligence of the driver of the bus.

At that time,
the documents produced by the claimant i.e., FIR - Ex.P1 and charge sheet - Ex.P9 it reveals that the accident was occurred due to negligent driving of the BMTC bus driver, but not the rider of the motor cycle.
The spot sketch also produced as per Ex.P4, which reveals that the bus driver was tried to overtake the motor cycle and caused the accident.

The respondent driver was not challenged the charge sheet before the Court for quashing the charge sheet against him and also not led any evidence of the inmates of the bus to show NC: 2024:KHC:21371 that there is no negligence on his part.
In this case, the tribunal has rightly held that this accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the BMTC bus driver but not due to rider of the motor cycle.
Therefore, there is no need to interfere in the findings of the tribunal in issue No.1 and due to which, the petitioner is the pillion rider sustained injuries in the accident.
13. As regards the quantum of compensation, the tribunal considered the injuries that the claimant suffered from grievous injuries, crush injury and fracture on the upper arm.

Therefore, Rs.30,000/-
awarded towards 'Pain and suffering' which is appropriate and no need to reduce the same.
14. As regards the medical expenses of Rs.1,27,937/- awarded by the tribunal, which is based upon the documents and evidence, need not be interfered.

15. With regards to the 'transportation, nourishment, conveyance and attendant charges', the NC:
2024:KHC:21371 tribunal has awarded a compensation of Rs.11,000/- which is just and proper and the same remains unaltered.
16. With regard to the 'future medical expenses', the tribunal has awarded a compensation of Rs.35,000/-.
The doctor has also not opined for further treatment and hence, the same need not be interfered.
17. As regards the 'loss of future amenities', the tribunal has awarded a compensation of Rs.12,000/-, which cannot be excessive and exorbitant and hence, need not be interfered.
18. As regards the 'computation of loss of income due to disability', the doctor - PW.2 has stated that the petitioner suffering from disability of 39% to the right arm and 13% to the whole body.
Though the learned counsel for the appellant seriously contended that the doctor who assessed the disability is not a treated doctor and it is not in accordance with the guidelines.

Ex.P15 - clinical examination report produced by the claimant and issued The Managing Director vs Smt. Chandrika. M on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145611409/
4 - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:21371 by PW.2, which reveals that the doctor though not treated the claimant, but he has assessed the disability, as per the guidelines in detail, he has given table in respect of disability with regard to the percentage.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 19. On perusal of the disability certificate it appears to be in scientific method each and every aspect has been considered and given certificate stating that there was 39% of the disability to the upper arm and to the whole body 13%.
The tribunal considered only 11% of disability instead of 13% stated by the doctor.
Therefore, there is no question of reducing further disability.
Income considered by the tribunal is R.15,000/- p.m. as notional income.
Even in the lok-adalath, the Court has considered Rs.15,000/- p.m. for the injuries sustained by him.
The accident occurred in the year 2021.
Therefore, the same is need not be interfered.
The age of the petitioner is considered as 25 years at the time of accident.
The multiplier applicable is '18'.
The tribunal has awarded Rs.3,56,4000/- (Rs.15,000/- X 12 X 18 X 11%) towards - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:21371 'loss of future income', which is not excessive and exorbitant.
Considering the same, there is no error committed by the tribunal in awarding compensation under the head loss of future income.
Hence, the appeal is devoid of merits and liable to be dismissed.

20 . Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER
The appeal is dismissed.
The statutory amount deposited to be  transmitted to the tribunal.

Sd/-
 JUDGE SSB The Managing Director vs Smt. Chandrika.
